name: StarSling

free.conditions: No credit card; first month only; unused minutes do not roll over.

caveats: GitHub Actions/Review Runners, not always-on generic VM (engine classifies the "ci" regime as a CI runner, so non-CI workloads see it as a different kind of product; no alt flag). Ubuntu 24.04, 5th-gen AMD EPYC. Advertised unlimited concurrency; job/session maximum not verified.
GPU rates include 4 vCPU/16 GB/100 GB host, not add-on rates. GPU access requires contacting provider; H100 coming soon, excluded from numerical rate list.
Do not apply advertised performance/TFLOPS savings as universal wall-clock discounts.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.
2,000 free runner minutes in the first month (no card; no rollover).

fleet.notes: CI/Review Runner product advertises unlimited concurrency, not a numerical resource guarantee. New signup includes 2,000 minutes without card. Numeric GPU allocation and large-fleet admission not published; GPU access may require contacting provider.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: A machine is provisioned when your job is queued and destroyed when the job finishes. There is no reuse across jobs, no warm pool of shared runners, and nothing — filesystem, image cache, process, or credential — carries from one job to the next.
snapshot_auto.note: These are single-use, ephemeral GitHub Actions runners: no state is saved.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Your job's filesystem, including the checkout — destroyed with the machine. Nothing is copied off it.
snapshot_on_demand.note: The API and CLI are read-only CI analytics (runs, jobs, logs, why, time, usage, bill). There is no snapshot or checkpoint call. Caching is done through GitHub's actions/cache: 'StarSling operates no separate cache or artifact store.'

harness_api.quote: The StarSling control plane exposes an HTTP API for everything the platform knows about your CI: which runs and jobs executed, why one failed, where the wall-clock went, and what it all cost.
harness_api.note: StarSling's own 'AI agents' run on StarSling's side and open CI-optimization PRs; they are not a harness you drive inside the runner. The sling CLI is 'agent-first' only in the sense that coding agents can call it to read CI data. Nothing starts or streams Claude Code, Codex or similar inside a runner.

guest_firewall.note: Per the data-handling page, 'On our sandbox providers a CPU job runs in a microVM; on our EC2 fleet ... your job runs in a privileged container *on its own dedicated instance*'. GPU tiers are containers on a dedicated machine. As a drop-in ubuntu-latest replacement, the runner presumably has sudo (not stated explicitly), so iptables/nftables inside works.

secret_proxy.quote: The runner itself is our machine. Secrets are in memory and on disk on the VM while your job runs. What protects them there is that the machine is single-use and destroyed with the job, not that the values never arrived.
secret_proxy.note: GitHub injects Actions secrets straight into the runner as env vars. There is no credential-injecting proxy.

isolation.quote: A machine boundary between customers. No two customers' jobs ever share a host. On our sandbox providers a CPU job runs in a microVM; on our EC2 fleet a job gets a dedicated instance that terminates when the job ends.
isolation.note: Docs only say 'microVM' on the sandbox-provider path (and a dedicated EC2 instance on the other path); the exact hypervisor is not named, but firecracker is the standard microVM tech behind CI-runner-as-a-service products, so this is a best-fit guess, not a direct claim.

image_oci.quote: StarSling uses structured labels to specify runner configuration. ... All sizes run Ubuntu 24.04 on 5th Gen AMD EPYC.
image_oci.note: not offered: runners are fixed Ubuntu 24.04 images selected by label; no documented way to boot from a customer-supplied Docker/OCI image.

docker_inside.note: Docs discuss 'Docker builds', 'Docker health checks' and Docker layer caching as normal CI steps on these runners, consistent with GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest images (which ship Docker); no explicit 'Docker is preinstalled' statement was found.

desktop.quote: AI-native CI for GitHub Actions: drop-in Ubuntu runners plus agents that open optimization PRs for your workflows.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (headless CI runner, not a desktop/VM product).

browser.quote: AI-native CI for GitHub Actions: drop-in Ubuntu runners plus agents that open optimization PRs for your workflows.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Workflows may install a browser like Playwright as a test dependency, but StarSling does not provide/manage a browser itself.

computer_use.quote: AI-native CI for GitHub Actions: drop-in Ubuntu runners plus agents that open optimization PRs for your workflows.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (CI runner, no screenshot/click driving API).

anti_bot.quote: AI-native CI for GitHub Actions: drop-in Ubuntu runners plus agents that open optimization PRs for your workflows.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (CI runner product, not a browsing/scraping product).

captcha_solving.quote: AI-native CI for GitHub Actions: drop-in Ubuntu runners plus agents that open optimization PRs for your workflows.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: On our sandbox providers a CPU job runs in a microVM; on our EC2 fleet a job gets a dedicated instance that terminates when the job ends.
egress_ip_type.note: Runners are backed by cloud/datacenter compute (own EC2 fleet plus third-party sandbox providers); no residential/mobile egress is offered or implied.

ssh.quote: Standard workflow logs are available in GitHub ... Look for the "Set up job" step ... Note the runner ID for support requests.
ssh.note: not offered: no SSH access to the runner is documented anywhere; debugging is via GitHub Actions logs and support tickets, consistent with a single-use, destroyed-on-completion machine.

snapshot.quote: A machine is provisioned when your job is queued and destroyed when the job finishes. There is no reuse across jobs, no warm pool of shared runners, and nothing — filesystem, image cache, process, or credential — carries from one job to the next.

fork.quote: A machine is provisioned when your job is queued and destroyed when the job finishes. There is no reuse across jobs, no warm pool of shared runners, and nothing ... carries from one job to the next.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (ephemeral single-use CI runner with no clone/fork API).

fork_running.quote: A machine is provisioned when your job is queued and destroyed when the job finishes.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; see fork.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: A machine is provisioned when your job is queued and destroyed when the job finishes.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; see fork.

pause_resume.quote: A machine is provisioned when your job is queued and destroyed when the job finishes.
pause_resume.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; single-use runner is destroyed, not paused.

wake_on_request.quote: A machine is provisioned when your job is queued and destroyed when the job finishes.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; a fresh runner is provisioned per queued job, there is no sleeping machine that wakes.

persistent_disk.quote: Your job's filesystem, including the checkout — destroyed with the machine. Nothing is copied off it.

volume_attach.quote: Your job's filesystem, including the checkout — destroyed with the machine. Nothing is copied off it.
volume_attach.note: not offered: no attachable persistent-volume feature documented; caching goes through GitHub's actions/cache instead.

volume_shared.quote: There is no reuse across jobs, no warm pool of shared runners, and nothing ... carries from one job to the next.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

live_resize.quote: The numeric suffix on a base label indicates the vCPU count (e.g. `-8` = 8 vCPU). The label without a suffix is the 4 vCPU default.
live_resize.note: not offered: size is fixed per runner label chosen in the workflow (a new machine per job), no API to resize a running machine.

agent_harnesses.quote: The StarSling control plane exposes an HTTP API for everything the platform knows about your CI: which runs and jobs executed, why one failed, where the wall-clock went, and what it all cost.
agent_harnesses.note: StarSling's own AI agents run on StarSling's side to open CI-optimization PRs; they are not a coding-agent harness preinstalled or offered as a template inside the runner.

own_agent_api.quote: AI agents that continuously analyze your workflows and open optimization PRs you review and merge.
own_agent_api.note: The optimization agents work autonomously on the control-plane side against your repo/workflows; there is no first-party API to drive them interactively (prompt/stream/follow-up) as a task agent.

lang_python.note: As a drop-in replacement for GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest/24.04 runners, the image is expected to carry the same general-purpose toolchain (Python, Node, etc.) as those images; not separately itemized in the docs.

lang_node.note: Same reasoning as lang_python; docs also show setup-node usage directly against StarSling runners in troubleshooting examples.

inbound_https.quote: AI-native CI for GitHub Actions: drop-in Ubuntu runners plus agents that open optimization PRs for your workflows.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. A CI runner executes a job and exits; there is no documented feature to expose an HTTPS URL to a port on the runner (the Tailscale integration is for outbound/private access, not inbound exposure).

ingress_rules.quote: AI-native CI for GitHub Actions: drop-in Ubuntu runners plus agents that open optimization PRs for your workflows.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; see inbound_https.

egress_allowlist.quote: By connecting StarSling Runners to your Tailscale network, your CI jobs get secure access to private services ... without exposing them to the public internet or maintaining static IP allow lists.
egress_allowlist.note: The Tailscale integration is offered explicitly as an alternative to static IP allowlisting (i.e. to avoid needing one on the customer's side); no provider-side outbound allow/deny or no-internet mode for the runner itself is documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: By connecting StarSling Runners to your Tailscale network, your CI jobs get secure access to private services — databases, NFS volumes, internal APIs — without exposing them to the public internet or maintaining static IP allow lists.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: no HTTP method/path-level egress rules documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: without exposing them to the public internet or maintaining static IP allow lists.
static_egress_ip.note: Tailscale is offered as the way to reach private resources precisely because there is no fixed/static outbound IP to allowlist; no static egress IP feature is documented.

windows.quote: Linux runners only today (no macOS or Windows runners). ... StarSling runners are Ubuntu/Linux only; macOS and Windows jobs stay on GitHub-hosted runners.

macos.quote: Linux runners only today (no macOS or Windows runners). ... StarSling runners are Ubuntu/Linux only; macOS and Windows jobs stay on GitHub-hosted runners.

arm64.note: Appears in StarSling's own comparison tables against competitors that do offer arm64/Windows/macOS; StarSling's own column is consistently 'Ubuntu 24.04 Linux runners' only, all on 5th Gen AMD EPYC (x64).

self_host.quote: Simple, transparent pricing for StarSling Runners
self_host.note: not offered: StarSling is a hosted SaaS (control plane + managed runner fleet / EC2); no self-hosted deployment of the StarSling platform itself is documented (distinct from GitHub's own self-hosted-runner concept, which StarSling explicitly positions itself as an alternative to).

byoc.quote: Simple, transparent pricing for StarSling Runners
byoc.note: not offered: no bring-your-own-cloud deployment option is documented; StarSling runs its own EC2 fleet and sandbox-provider capacity.

open_source.quote: ci-speedup skill: a free, open-source (MIT) skill that audits a repository's GitHub Actions workflows ... Runs locally, no account needed.
open_source.note: Only StarSling's ancillary CLI 'skills' (ci-speedup, ci-score, ci-secure) are open source (MIT); the core runner/control-plane product itself is closed-source SaaS.

hipaa.quote: SOC 2 Type II ... Status: In progress ... ISO 27001 ... Status: In progress ... Enterprise Security Features Available for Enterprise: Single Sign-On (SSO) via SAML, Audit log export, Custom data retention policies, Dedicated support channel, Security review calls.
hipaa.note: HIPAA/BAA is not listed among current or in-progress certifications/enterprise features; only SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 (both in progress) are mentioned.

nested_virt.quote: On our sandbox providers a CPU job runs in a microVM; on our EC2 fleet a job gets a dedicated instance that terminates when the job ends... on the EC2 path your job runs in a privileged container *on its own dedicated instance*
nested_virt.note: StarSling Runners are a drop-in ubuntu-latest/ubuntu-24.04 GitHub Actions replacement; jobs run in a microVM or a privileged container on a dedicated instance, not a bare-metal/full-VM host with /dev/kvm exposed. No docs mention nested virtualization or KVM device passthrough; not offered on this CI-runner product.

mcp_server.quote: The StarSling control plane exposes an HTTP API for everything the platform knows about your CI: which runs and jobs executed, why one failed, where the wall-clock went, and what it all cost.
mcp_server.note: StarSling ships an HTTP API and the 'sling' CLI (agent-first, i.e. readable/callable by coding agents) but no MCP server. Checked the docs (llms-full.txt has no 'MCP'/'Model Context Protocol' mentions) and the starslingdev GitHub org (repos: openai-agents-python, skills, keep, terraform-aws-github-runner, hpc-sandbox-benchmarks — no mcp-server repo).

public_ipv4.quote: By connecting StarSling Runners to your Tailscale network, your CI jobs get secure access to private services — databases, NFS volumes, internal APIs — without exposing them to the public internet or maintaining static IP allow lists.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. StarSling Runners are single-use, destroyed-on-completion GitHub Actions CI runners meant to execute a job and exit; there is no product surface for exposing/reaching a runner via an inbound public IPv4 address, and the docs frame reachability the other way (runner reaching your private network via Tailscale).

eu_data_residency.quote: Control plane | US East ... Runners | US East (more regions coming) ... Logs | US East
eu_data_residency.note: All control plane, runner, and log data is located in US East only today ('more regions coming' implies no EU region yet). The pricing page lists 'Custom security or data residency requirements' as an Enterprise custom-agreement item, not a shipped EU region.

soc2.quote: SOC 2 Type II Status: In progress. We are actively working toward SOC 2 Type II certification. Expected completion: Q1 2027.
soc2.note: Not yet certified as of check date; compliance page explicitly states SOC 2 Type II is in progress, expected Q1 2027, so false is correct.
